annotations.shape: a multipart/digest (boundary b0-headerless-digest-20250304) whose single child declares NO Content-Type header at all
annotations.rfc_basis: RFC 2046 section 5.1.5: the body parts of a multipart/digest are themselves message/rfc822 unless their Content-Type says otherwise, so the header-less child is a message, not text. RFC 2045 section 5.2's text/plain default does NOT apply to it. This is the recorded disagreement (a FINDING of Turn 1.12): the walker records content_type null and runs its text charset ladder over the child (used_charset us-ascii), so its recorded reading is text; the RFC's effective media type is message/rfc822. The default is supplied as a projection over the raw field (emailextract/mediatype.py), never as a rewrite of the walker's record, and the gap body.digest_default_not_applied names it.
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was typed by a model from the RFC rules and read out of the fixture bytes (a byte/offset listing); never produced by running the library. labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person.
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, part.tree, part.gaps, decode.chain and body.content_sha256 -- the walker's reading, which records content_type null and never an invented default.
annotations.phase_1_facts: document.axes, the attachment stage's attach.manifest/attach.types (the child is an occurrence: it is not a displayable view) and the gaps.later row for body.digest_default_not_applied.
annotations.not_yet_labelled: headers.fields, part.regions and body.preamble_epilogue are not typed here; phases 2 and 3 are not exercised.

value: the child has no Content-Type and is message/rfc822 by RFC 2046 5.1.5, but the walker records content_type null; the default is a projection over the raw field, never a rewrite of it (design D3, emailextract/mediatype.py)

the RFC makes a header-less multipart/digest child message/rfc822 (RFC 2046 5.1.5), so per the RFC it has no text view; the walker runs its text ladder and would report a decoded text. This label types only the walker's recorded decode chain and leaves the body text open -- the recorded walker/RFC disagreement.

whether a message/rfc822 digest child has quote boundaries is not an RFC question this turn settles: the RFC says the part is a message, the walker reads it as text with no quoting constructs. Left open rather than typed.
as for body.quote_boundaries: the RFC gives the child no text view, so it has no view level; the walker would produce one. Left open as part of the same recorded disagreement.
